pr.title: coverage: Re-enable `UnreachablePropagation` for coverage builds
pr.description:
This is a sequence of 3 related changes:
- Clean up the existing code that scans for unused functions
- Detect functions that were instrumented for coverage, but have had all their coverage statements removed by later MIR transforms (e.g. `UnreachablePropagation`)
- Re-enable `UnreachablePropagation` in coverage builds

Because we now detect functions that have lost their coverage statements, and treat them as unused, we don't need to worry about `UnreachablePropagation` removing all of those statements. This is demonstrated by `tests/coverage/unreachable.rs`.

Fixes #116171.
pr.author: Zalathar

issues.title: Make coverage robust against MIR optimizations removing all counter-increment statements
issues.body:
When coverage instrumentation and MIR opts are both enabled, coverage relies on two assumptions:

- MIR opts that would delete `StatementKind::Coverage` statements instead move them into bb0 and change them to `CoverageKind::Unreachable`.

- MIR opts won't delete all `CoverageKind::Counter statements` from an instrumented function.

The first assumption will be lifted by #116046, which stores coverage mappings in a separate per-function struct, so the original mappings will be available during codegen even if MIR opts delete arbitrary coverage statements.

---

The second assumption is trickier. If a function is instrumented for coverage, but MIR opts remove *all* of its counter-increment statements (e.g. because bb0's ends with `TerminatorKind::Unreachable`), then we will codegen a function with no `llvm.instrprof.increment` intrinsics. This causes LLVM to assume that the function wasn't instrumented, so it will disappear from the final coverage mappings and won't participate in coverage reports.

Coverage has special code for handling functions that are deemed “unused” at the MIR level, but if a function *is* used (e.g. as a function pointer) but its body is unreachable, then that special code isn't applied.

---

Ideally what we need is some way for coverage codegen to detect that an instrumented function has no remaining counter-increment statements, and take special action to either re-insert at least one counter-increment (so LLVM treats it as instrumented), or treat it as though it were unused (so that it shows up in reports as never-executed).

---

analysis.summary: Re-enabling `UnreachablePropagation` under `-C instrument-coverage` requires coverage codegen to treat an instrumented function that has lost all of its own coverage statements as "unused" (Code(Zero)), even when that function still participates in codegen. Otherwise the function keeps a live counter mapping but LLVM sees no increment intrinsic and silently drops it from coverage reports.
analysis.originalLogic: `UnreachablePropagation::is_enabled` ran only when `sess.mir_opt_level() >= 2 && !sess.instrument_coverage()`, with the FIXME comment that coverage gets confused by MIR passes that remove all coverage statements. Unused-function detection in `mapgen.rs` treated a function as unused only if it was function-like, absent from `all_mono_items`, and not `used_via_inlining`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Running `UnreachablePropagation` on a coverage-instrumented function whose body is unreachable deletes all of that function's own `StatementKind::Coverage` statements/counter increments. If coverage codegen still classifies the function as "used" merely because it participates in codegen, it emits a live `Counter(0)` mapping without any `llvm.instrprof.increment` intrinsic, so LLVM "assume[s] that the function wasn't instrumented" and the function disappears from the final coverage mappings. The correct behavior is to detect the instrumented-but-no-own-coverage function and emit it as unused, with `Code(Zero)` instead of `Code(Counter(0))`.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust programs compiled with coverage instrumentation (e.g. `-C instrument-coverage`) and MIR optimizations at level 2 (`-Zmir-opt-level=2`), containing a function-like item (fn/assoc fn/closure) that has `function_coverage_info` but whose body is entirely unreachable (e.g. ends in the `unreachable` intrinsic / `TerminatorKind::Unreachable`), optionally reachable via a function pointer so a codegen stub is produced.
analysis.trigger: `UnreachablePropagation` removes every coverage statement that belongs to an instrumented function (all counter increments are gone), while the function still appears among codegen mono items.
preconditions: the function is function-like and carries function_coverage_info
all of the function's own (non-inlined) coverage statements were removed by later MIR transforms
the function still participates directly in codegen, e.g. as a function pointer target or an emitted unreachable stub
pitfalls: Classifying unused functions only by `all_mono_items` membership misses instrumented functions that lost all coverage statements but still codegen
Treating any missing coverage as inlined is wrong; non-inlined coverage statements belong to the enclosing function, so track `saw_own_coverage` separately from `used_via_inlining`
Do not conflate inlined-into coverage with own coverage: a function with coverage statements in other functions cannot simply be marked unused
A function with no coverage statements and no `function_coverage_info` was never instrumented and must be skipped, not marked unused
analysis.testStrategy: Use the existing `tests/coverage/unreachable.rs` cov-map test compiled with coverage instrumentation and MIR opt level 2. Construct two inputs differing only in reachability: (A) a reachable instrumented function that retains its counter increment, expected `Code(Counter(0))`; (B) the same function made fully unreachable so `UnreachablePropagation` removes all its coverage statements. The corrected map must label the function `(unused)` and map it to `Code(Zero)`; the historically wrong output keeps `Code(Counter(0))` (and the function effectively vanishes). Inspect the `.cov-map` diff: `unreachable::unreachable_intrinsic (unused)` and `Code(Zero) at (prev + 22, 1)`. No compiler was executed here.
